recipes.name: Monster Cookies
ingredients: 1 cup plain flour / all-purpose flour ((Note 1 for gluten-free))
1 tsp baking soda ((bi-carbonate soda), sifted if lumpy (Note 3))
1/4 tsp cooking salt / kosher salt ((halve for table salt, +50% for flakes))
125g/ 8 tbsp unsalted butter (, cut into chunks (for even melting) (also see Note 5 on butter measure))
3/4 cup creamy peanut butter NOT natural peanut butter
1 large egg ((~50-55g/2oz in shell), fridge cold is fine)
1 cup (200g) M&Ms (, plain chocolate ones, not peanut or crispy rice - or smarties!)
1/2 cup (90g) dark chocolate chips / semi-sweet chips
2 tbsp (20g) dark chocolate chips / semi-sweet chips
instructions: Mix Dry ingredients in a bowl (with wooden spoon). Barely melt butter, finish melting by hand. Add remaining Wet, mix. Mix in Dry, adding choc chips and M&M's towards the end. Roll 18 x 3 tbsp balls (size 20 cookie scoop), bake 15 min @ 180°C/350°F (160°C fan), cool 10 min on tray then 10 min on rack before attacking!
Preheat the oven to 180°C/350°F (160°C fan-forced). Line 3 trays with baking paper (parchment paper).
Dry ingredients - Put the Dry ingredients in a medium bowl and mix with a wooden spoon, just to combine.

Barely melt butter – Put the butter in a microwave proof bowl and microwave in 20 second increments on high until almost melted. Then mix with a wooden spoon to finish melting using residual heat. (Note 4)
Wet ingredients - To the butter bowl, add the rest of the Wet ingredients. Then mix vigorously with the wooden spoon until it's smooth.

Make cookie dough - Add the Dry ingredients in, then mix until most of the flour is mixed in. Then add the chocolate chips and M&M's, then mix until they are dispersed through the batter and you can no longer see flour.

Roll cookie balls - Roll* into 18 balls, 3 tablespoons each (4.5cm / 1.8" diameter). My method - portion all dough using size 20 cookie scoop, then roll. Place balls on three paper lined trays at least 7.5cm / 3" apart.* If dough is a bit too sticky to roll, pop in fridge for 5 min, firms up quickly.
Bake 2 trays for 15 minutes, switching the tray shelves at the 8 minute mark.

Decorate (optional) - While the cookies are still hot, press chocolate chips onto the surface (the heat will melt them enough to stick) and lightly press M&M’s halfway in, they’ll set firmly in place once the cookies cool. (Note 5).

Cool for 10 minutes on the tray (to finish cooking and set) then transfer to a rack and cool for another 10 minutes before attacking, these cookies are fragile when hot. (Meanwhile, bake the third tray). Fully cool before storing in an airtight container for 5 days, in a cool pantry.

page_recipe_notes: Recipe Notes: 1. Gluten-free- For gluten free: Use gluten-free flour and uncontaminated/pure rolled oats (sold as “wheat free” oats in Australia). Note that under Australian food standards, oats cannot be labelled gluten free. 2. Oat – Just plain rolled oats. Not not steel-cut, quick cooking or those sweetened/flavoured porridge sachets! (Edit: Actually, plain quick cooking oats are probably ok, I haven’t tried but see no reason why they would not work). 3. Baking soda (bi-carbonate soda) – These make the cookies rise as well as spread a bit so they don’t end up like chunky rock cakes. You can substituted with 2 teaspoons of baking powder but expect them to be thicker and not spread quite as much. 4. Peanut butter type matters! These cookies MUST be made with regular peanut butter spread, the type with sugar, salt, oil etc added (check ingredients). Popular brands – Bega (Australia), Jif, Skippy (US), Sun-Pat (UK). It won’t work with natural peanut butter (ie, the runnier type with no added sugar, or oil to prevent separation, and often no salt either), the dough and cookie will be dry and crumbly. 5. Barely melted butter – I like using this method where you finish melting by mixing and using the residual heat, the butter is cooler and a little thicker so prevents the need to wait until the butter cools before adding other ingredients in, or chilling the dough. 6. M&M decorative topping – Push them halfway into the warm cookies, they will adhere as the cookie cools. You have to do this while the cookie is warm, when the surface is still pliable. If the cookies cool too much, just press them onto a melty choc chip instead – edible glue! 7. Different measures in different countries – US cups are slightly smaller (236ml vs 250ml), which can matter in baking. I tested this recipe using US cups, Australian cups and the weights provided, and all worked the same. Butter note: 8 tbsp is technically 113g (1 US stick), not 125g, but this small difference does not affect the recipe. 8 tbsp is a neat measure! Storage – Fully cool then store in an airtight container in the pantry for up to 4 days. You can also refrigerate the cookie balls (make sure they are in a very airtight container), bake per recipe rom fridge cold, adding a couple of minutes to the bake time. The cookie balls can also be frozen, add 3 minutes to the bake time. Nutrition per cookie.
